t: A roomier, faster 8-bit chip for Arduino-style sensor and LED projects.
steps: Buy an AVR128DA48 Curiosity Nano from an electronics distributor, or an Azduino breakout from Tindie.
Install the free Arduino IDE on your computer.
Add the DxCore board package through the Boards Manager.
Pick a part from the AVR128DA or AVR64DA lines. Early AVR32DA chips have a known defect.
Make a SerialUPDI link from a USB serial adapter and a small diode.
Choose your chip in the board menu and pick SerialUPDI as the programmer.
Open the Blink example and press Upload. An LED on your board starts to blink.
